title: Residential Property Disclosure Form
description: Ohio requires sellers of residential real property to complete the Residential Property Disclosure Form prescribed by the Ohio Division of Real Estate. The form covers structural systems, water supply, sewer, roof, insulation, hazardous materials, and other known conditions. Must be delivered to the buyer before the purchase agreement is signed or within three days of entering into the agreement.

required_actions.note: Buyer may rescind the purchase agreement within 3 days of receiving the disclosure if it reveals new material information.

title: Agency Disclosure Statement
description: Ohio licensees must provide a written Agency Disclosure Statement at the first substantive contact with a buyer or seller. The statement must disclose whether the licensee represents the buyer, seller, or both (dual agency). Dual agency is permitted with written informed consent of both parties.

title: Closing Type — Title Company or Attorney
description: Ohio residential closings may be conducted by title companies, escrow agents, or attorneys. There is no statutory requirement for attorney involvement, though it is common in some regions of the state. Title insurance is customary and typically arranged through a title company.

required_actions.note: Title company or attorney may conduct closing. Practice varies by region.

title: Lead Hazard Notification and Abatement
description: Ohio has additional state-level lead paint requirements beyond the federal mandate. The Ohio Residential Lead-Based Paint Abatement Act requires notification to occupants of known lead hazards. For rental properties, landlords must provide lead-safe certifications. For sales of pre-1978 homes, disclosure is mandatory under both federal and Ohio law.

required_actions.note: Ohio adds state-level lead hazard notification requirements per ORC §3742.

title: Real Property Conveyance Fee
description: Ohio imposes a mandatory county conveyance fee on the transfer of real property. The state portion is $1 per $1,000 of the sale price. Counties may impose an additional permissive fee of up to $3 per $1,000. The conveyance fee statement must be filed with the county auditor at closing.

required_actions.note: Filed with county auditor at closing. Paid by seller unless otherwise agreed.
